title: Ashlynne Mike AMBER Alert in Indian Country Act
official_summary:
Ashlynne Mike AMBER Alert in Indian Country Act

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the PROTECT Act to reauthorize the AMBER Alert grant program for FY2019.

The bill also modifies the program to:

  • add, as a new purpose area, the integration of tribal AMBER Alert systems into state AMBER alert systems;
  • make Indian tribes eligible for AMBER Alert grants;
  • permit the use of grant funds to integrate state or regional AMBER Alert communication plans with an Indian tribe; and
  • allow the waiver of the matching funds requirement for grants awarded to Indian tribes.

(Sec. 3) The Department of Justice must submit to Congress a report evaluating the readiness, education, and training needs, technological challenges, and specific obstacles encountered by Indian tribes in the integration of state or regional AMBER Alert communication plans.

summary.headline: This law makes Indian tribes eligible for AMBER Alert grants and helps link tribal alert systems with state systems.
summary.what_it_does: It amends the PROTECT Act to renew the AMBER Alert grant program for fiscal year 2019. It adds linking tribal AMBER Alert systems with state systems as a new purpose for the grants. Tribes can now apply for these grants, and grant money can be used to connect state or regional alert plans with a tribe. The Justice Department must also report to Congress on the readiness, training, technology, and other obstacles tribes face in joining these systems.

who_it_affects.how: Tribes become eligible to receive AMBER Alert grants and may use them to connect with state or regional alert plans.

who_it_affects.group: State and regional AMBER Alert programs
who_it_affects.how: They can use grant funds to coordinate communication plans with neighboring tribes.

who_it_affects.group: Families of missing children on tribal lands
who_it_affects.how: Alerts may reach tribal communities more directly once tribal systems are linked to state systems.
It must study and report to Congress on the challenges tribes face in joining state alert systems.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted April 13, 2018; the grant program reauthorization applies to fiscal year 2019.
